best_for: Type designers, students and developers who need to build, fix or convert fonts without paying for a commercial font editor, and who like to script repetitive work.
description:
FontForge is a font editor first written by George Williams and now kept up by a community of type lovers, who welcome help from people who do not write code. A font editor works like a drawing program, except you draw a shape for every letter and then tell the program how those shapes fit together.

You can open, edit and convert fonts in OpenType, TrueType, PostScript, UFO, CID-keyed and Multiple Master formats, and generate bitmap versions. Set the spacing between letters, and add ligatures, such as the rule that joins f and i into one shape. If you are new to this, the online manual Design With FontForge walks you through making a font, and the mailing list and the #fontforge chat on Libera answer questions.

points.title: A full font editor at no cost
points.text: FontForge is a free and open source font editor under the GPL 3. You design or repair fonts in it and keep your work in its own SFD project format, then export fonts such as TTF.

points.title: Scriptable in Python
points.text: You can drive it from Python or its own scripting language, so batch jobs like renaming glyphs or regenerating a family run without clicking. Command-line helpers such as `fontlint`, `sfddiff` and `fontimage` come with it.

points.title: The October 2025 release
points.text: Release 20251009 moved to Unicode 17, allows emoji and other supplementary-plane characters in SFD files and TTF export, and adds HarfBuzz shaping to the Metrics View. It also removed the old X11 drawing backend.

points.title: Mac needs a manual first launch
points.text: The Mac download page has you move the app to Applications, then right-click it and choose Open to confirm the first launch. Homebrew has disabled its FontForge app cask after it failed the Gatekeeper check. The DMG listed here is universal and marked for macOS 13 or later.

points.title: Linux: Flatpak is community-built
points.text: The project recommends its own AppImage for Linux and warns that distro packages are often outdated. The Flatpak listed here is not verified on Flathub, so it is packaged by the community rather than confirmed as the project's.

points.title: Few versions to roll back to
points.text: This site keeps 3 Windows versions, each a machine-wide x64 installer, and only the current release on Mac and Linux.
